newsitem.title: USA: High-octane gasoline NYH market surges on outages.
newsitem.headline: High-octane gasoline NYH market surges on outages.

text.p: The usually dormant high-octane premium gasoline market in the New York Harbor has sprung to life in recent days, prodded by a number of outages at key refineries.

Though downed gasoline units at the Lagoven (PDVSA) Amuay refinery in Venezuela and at Sun Co Inc's Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania plant are up or about to come back up, work at the giant Amerada Hess refinery in the Virgin Islands has weeks to ru. Also, the lagged effect of the refinery down-time on the market is expected to keep upward pressure on prices, traders said.
"The price spike is the collective impact of several weeks of refinery maintenance," said one East Coast gasoline trader.

Prices for conventional and reformulated 93-octane unleaded in New York Harbor have shot up by about 10 cents in the past two weeks, with a jump of nearly four cents on Thursday alone to 80.40 cents a gallon. The premium for physical product over the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) gasoline contract has more than doubled to almost 11.50 cents, its highest since May, 1995.

The availability of high octane blending components like reformate or aromatics used to turn regular 87-octane unleaded into 93-octane unleaded gasoline are hard to come by these days, particularly in New York Harbor, traders said.
"I can't find find blendstocks anywhere," another trader said, noting refinery outages on the East Coast are contributing to the tightness in New York Harbor.
"Obviously, Hess is a very big factor up there," the trader said.

Lagoven's Amuay restarted its damaged 105,000 barrel per day (bpd) cat cracker Thursday and it was near normal production on Friday. Also, Sun's 85,000 bpd cat is set to come up over the weekend. But Hess is not expected to be finished with its upgrade, which will bring the cracker's capacity to 125,000 bpd, until mid-December.

Traders noted that while cat crackers produce a relatively low quality, low octane "cat gasoline," such units also produce feedstocks to make high octane blendstocks, such as the aromatic tolulene, that are in turn used to make premium.
"A lot of the duration of the price spike is contingent on whether those refinery restarts go smoothly," the East Coast trader said.

Also, the lagged effect of the outages is likely to keep the market tight for a while after the units are back up. It takes about a week to ship product up from Amuay to the harbor and alternative pipeline supplies from the Gulf of Mexico refiners takes around 18 days, traders noted.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
